title: Rigatoni alla Sorrentina
subtitle: Baked Italian pasta with tomato, mozzarella, and basil
excerpt: Rigatoni tossed with a quick tomato sauce, loaded with torn mozzarella, and finished under a hot oven until the cheese bubbles and browns in patches. A weeknight baked pasta that is ready in under 40 minutes.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla sorrentina takes its name from Sorrento on the Amalfi Coast, where the combination of tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil has been a kitchen staple for generations. The baked format is a Neapolitan adaptation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 2 hours ahead and keep at room temperature before baking.

content.text: Undercook the pasta by 2 minutes before it goes in the oven. It will finish cooking in the sauce and absorb the flavour as it bakes.

items.prepNote: torn into pieces and patted dry

content.text: Cook the rigatoni in heavily salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain, reserving a cup of pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a saucepan over a medium heat.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, crushing the tomatoes as they cook.
Stir in most of the basil.
Toss the drained pasta in the tomato sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Transfer to a baking dish. Scatter the mozzarella evenly over the top.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and spotted with brown.
Scatter the remaining basil over just before serving.

items.symptom: Pasta is dry and has absorbed all the sauce.
items.cause: Not enough sauce or pasta water was added before baking.
items.fix: Add a few more tablespoons of pasta water before it goes in the oven.

items.symptom: Mozzarella released a lot of water and made the dish soggy.
items.cause: The mozzarella was not patted dry before using.
items.fix: Tear and press between kitchen paper for a few minutes before adding.
